findings.text: follow-on: parsed_state is defined but has no caller anywhere in reckon/ or tests/ (grep finds only the definition), so it is dead code whose docstring promises a reuse of the shared per-file parse that never happens and it should be removed or wired up.

follow-on: the recorded arms do not share fail ids as the done_when requires — the base arm fails test_a_code_review_reads_its_projects_package::test_this_repository_reads_the_same_modules_as_the_reckon_listing while the head arm does not — and the stale chunk arm under logs/head (23:00, pre-commit) shows six head failures that the later all_head.log contradicts; the manifest records both logs without reconciling the difference, so a reader cannot tell which head arm is authoritative.

item_verdicts.diff: read 7b8fcb27 and 73155abc against base 2e26dc96 commit by commit; metadata_index gains a discovery map plus discovery_state/record_discovery/readiness_from_state/parsed_state, serve consumes it and delegates readiness to the owner, _plan_html gains reuse_parsed_state, and a 267-line test file is added.
item_verdicts.done_when: the gate names tests/test_a_fresh_process_reuses_the_plan_parse.py and the manifest records it; I re-ran that file at head and it reports 5 passed, but the recorded aggregate arms do not share fail ids as the done_when requires.
item_verdicts.goal: the node goal is to make a fresh process read each plan's parsed discovery and readiness from the persisted metadata index and re-parse only changed files; reckon/serve.py:2282 fetches metadata_index.discovery_state and :2301 seeds the shared parse from it, which is that deliverable.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it names commits 7b8fcb27 and 73155abc, the 74-file head arm (787 passed, 1 collection error), the base arm logs and the negative-control log, and its landed fragment.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares the five product/test/evidence paths plus a figures directory; the diff touches exactly those five and writes no figure, all inside the declared scope.

justifications.durability: with the declared mutation the negative control reddens three parse-count cases (negative_control_store_bypassed.log, 3 failed, EXIT=1), so tests/test_a_fresh_process_reuses_the_plan_parse.py:198 fails if the store is bypassed, and the count/status assertions are against constants and the file the test wrote, not against the value under test.
justifications.evidence: all_head.log records 787 passed/1 error and all_base.log records 1 failed/781 passed/1 error, so the base failing id (test_a_code_review_reads_its_projects_package::test_this_repository_reads_the_same_modules_as_the_reckon_listing) is absent at head and the manifest does not reconcile the parity the done_when asserts.
justifications.fit: the additions follow the module idiom (Mapping guards, field-comment style at reckon/metadata_index.py:94) and the naming scan finds no banned label, but reckon/metadata_index.py:775 ships an unused function.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/serve.py:2282 reads metadata_index.discovery_state and :2292-2301 reuses stored meta/readiness and seeds the parse, so an unchanged tree is served without a re-parse exactly as the goal states.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the owners it should — the persisted index and its rows in reckon/metadata_index.py:794 and :835, and the shared parse memo via reckon/_plan_html.py:1425 — with readiness logic moved to its owner at reckon/metadata_index.py:750 rather than duplicated.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff (reckon/serve.py, reckon/metadata_index.py, reckon/_plan_html.py, the new test, the fragment) is a declared write path, though reckon/metadata_index.py:775 adds parsed_state that the goal does not imply.
